title: When Helpful Advice Starts Sounding Like Criticism
summary: A simple three-step check to help parents give useful advice without turning it into another lecture.
seo_title: When Teen Advice Sounds Like Criticism
seo_description: When your teen hears criticism instead of help, use this simple three-step check to say less, keep clear boundaries, and hand back the next step.
release_move: Give the part they need. Keep the boundary that matters. Then let your teenager carry the next piece.

core_belief_shift.from: If my teenager rejects good advice, I need to explain it again until they understand.
core_belief_shift.to: My teenager may need one clear point, one firm boundary, and room to handle the next step.

book_relevance.reason: The article completes a parent reflection and ownership-transfer job; a Playbook bridge would add product pressure without serving the reader's immediate need.

hero.alt: A Polynesian father pauses at a front-porch railing while his teenage daughter sits below holding a folded school paper.

social_image.alt: A Polynesian father pauses at a front-porch railing while his teenage daughter sits below holding a folded school paper.

next_step.label: Turn the next argument into a useful conversation
next_step.reason: Use this next when advice has already become an argument and you need a calmer way back to understanding.
